lines.text: Morning! Can everyone hear me?
Yep, loud and clear.
Great. Let's go in the usual order, so Priyanka first, then Maximilian, then you, then I'll wrap with the release checklist.

So yesterday I finished the retry logic for the uploader. It now backs off from two seconds up to thirty, and the status line says how many lines are waiting. I tested it by pulling the network cable mid-call and every line made it to Postgres within a minute of plugging it back in.
Nice. How many lines was that?
About fifteen hundred from a forty minute call, and zero duplicates, because the segment ids are generated on the Mac.
Perfect.

Today I'm picking up IA-214, the one about the permission screen. The ticket is at https://linear.app/linkt/issue/IA-214/permission-screen-names-the-system-settings-pane-and-the-switch-to-flip if anyone wants to follow along.
No blockers from me.
Okay, Maximilian Okonkwo-Vandersloot here, sorry, my camera's being weird. I spent most of yesterday on the call audio helper.

The short version is that macOS pins the privacy grant to the code signature, so every ad-hoc build silently loses call audio even though System Settings still shows Roger switched on. With the stable signing identity it survives a quit and relaunch. I checked the tccd log and there's no 'Failed to match existing code requirement' line any more.
So the field report from Tuesday is fixed?
I think so, but I want one real thirty minute Meet call on the installed app before I say it out loud.
Fair. Can you do that today?
Yes, I've got the Northwind demo at two, I'll record that one. If it works I'll paste the stt meter line into the channel.
Great.

Okay, me. Yesterday I got the notes prompt down to about fifteen thousand tokens for an hour-long call, so a full call costs well under a cent with the current model. The citations come back as L-numbers and we map them to segment ids on the API side.
Today I'm on the long-call path: anything over the budget gets split into windows of whole lines with twenty lines of overlap, then one reduce pass merges them.
Does the reduce pass keep the citations?
It does, the refs stay global across windows. The reduce step just can't cite a line that no window cited, so it can't invent sources.
Makes sense.
No blockers, but I'd love a second pair of eyes on the eval report on Thursday.
I can do Thursday morning.
Thanks, Priyanka.

Alright, release checklist. One: AssemblyAI training opt-out is done in the dashboard, I have the screenshot. Two: the cost guards are on by default. Three: we still need the thirty minute real call logged in the M1 exit check before Rahul merges.
Maximilian's two o'clock covers number three if it goes well, so we could close M1 by end of day.
And if it doesn't go well?
Then we read the tccd log first, before touching any code. Nine times out of ten it's the grant, not us.
Ha. Okay, sounds like a plan.
Anything else? No? Thanks everyone, see you tomorrow.
Bye!
